summary.text: A giant hunter who wooed Merope on Chios, was blinded by her father Oenopion, recovered his sight at the sunrise, and was set among the stars after his death.

story.text: Orion went to Chios and wooed Merope, daughter of Oenopion; but the king made him drunk, put out his eyes as he slept, and cast him on the beach. Orion went to the smithy of Hephaestus, set a lad on his shoulders, and bade him lead him to the sunrise; being come thither he was healed by the sun's rays.

Homer knows him as a hunter even in death: on Calypso's isle Odysseus saw Orion driving wild beasts over the meadow of asphodel that he had himself slain on the lonely hills, bearing a bronze club unbreakable forever.

Hesiod's Astronomy tells how Orion was stung by the scorpion and died, and how Zeus set him in the sky as a constellation — the hunter who pursues the Pleiades and the Bear through all the nights of the year.
